title: Name length limit off by one: a name of exactly 100 characters is rejected
observable: POST /api/v1/users {"name": "<100 x 'a'>"} returns 422 {"error":"Validation failed","message":"name is too long"} instead of 201; no row is inserted.

title: Create silently trims surrounding whitespace from the name before inserting
observable: POST /api/v1/users {"name": "  Alice  "} returns 201, but GET /api/v1/users/{id} returns name "Alice" and the users row holds 'Alice' instead of '  Alice  '. A whitespace-only name "   " is stored as an empty string.

title: Control-character check lets tab and newline through
observable: POST /api/v1/users {"name": "Line1\nLine2"} (or containing \t) returns 201 and inserts the row instead of 422 {"error":"Validation failed","message":"name contains invalid characters"}. Same for PUT.

title: next_cursor emitted when the page is exactly full even with no further rows
observable: With exactly 3 users, GET /api/v1/users?limit=3 returns all 3 plus a non-empty next_cursor (should be omitted); following it returns 200 with data null and no next_cursor.

title: Keyset predicate uses >= so each page repeats the previous page's last row
observable: With users ids 1..5, GET /api/v1/users?limit=2 returns ids 1,2 with next_cursor; GET ?limit=2&cursor=<that> returns ids 2,3 instead of 3,4 (duplicate across pages, walk never covers set cleanly).
edits: WHERE id > $1 ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT $2
WHERE id >= $1 ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT $2

title: List ordered descending by id
observable: With ids 1..5, GET /api/v1/users returns ids in order 5,4,3,2,1 instead of 1..5; with ?limit=2 the second page (cursor after id 4) returns id 5 again instead of 3,4.

title: Over-cap limit clamped to the default page size instead of the maximum
observable: With 30 users, GET /api/v1/users?limit=150 returns only 20 items plus a next_cursor, instead of all 30 items (limit should clamp to 100).

title: Undecodable (non-base64) cursor maps to 500 instead of 400
observable: GET /api/v1/users?cursor=!!!notbase64 returns 500 {"error":"Database operation failure"} instead of 400 {"error":"Invalid pagination cursor"}.

title: Cursor that decodes to a non-numeric id is silently treated as the start of the list
observable: GET /api/v1/users?cursor=YWJj (base64url of "abc") returns 200 with the first page of users instead of 400 {"error":"Invalid pagination cursor"}. Same for a base64 of an out-of-range id such as "99999999999".

title: Deleting a nonexistent id reports success
observable: DELETE /api/v1/users/999999 (no such row) returns 200 {"message":"deleted user with ID of 999999 successfully"} instead of 404 {"error":"Not found"}. Deleting the same id twice returns 200 both times.

title: Update of a nonexistent user maps to 500 instead of 404
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/999999 {"name":"Bob"} returns 500 {"error":"Database operation failure"} instead of 404 {"error":"Not found"}. Also PUT /api/v1/users/abc.

title: PUT with empty or missing name treated as a no-op partial update
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/{existing id} with {} or {"name":""} returns 200 with the unchanged user instead of 422 {"error":"Validation failed","message":"name is required"}. PUT /api/v1/users/999999 {} returns 404 instead of 422.

title: ID parsed as 64-bit then truncated to int32, so large ids alias small ones
observable: With user id 1 present, GET /api/v1/users/4294967297 returns 200 with user 1 instead of 404; DELETE /api/v1/users/4294967297 deletes row id 1; PUT renames row id 1.

title: Non-numeric id on show returns 500 instead of 404
observable: GET /api/v1/users/abc (or /api/v1/users/1.5) returns 500 {"error":"Database operation failure"} instead of 404 {"error":"Not found"}.

title: Create returns 200 instead of 201
observable: POST /api/v1/users {"name":"Alice"} returns status 200 (body unchanged: message "Created user successfully", data "<id>") instead of 201 Created.

title: Show endpoint no longer sets Content-Type application/json
observable: GET /api/v1/users/{id} (200 and 404 responses) carries Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8 (sniffed) instead of application/json. Body is unchanged.

title: Bearer scheme compared case-sensitively
observable: GET /api/v1/users with "Authorization: bearer <valid token>" (or BEARER) returns 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} instead of 200; "Bearer <token>" still works.

title: Audience claim no longer validated
observable: A token signed with JWT_SECRET, correct iss and exp, but aud "some-other-service" (or no aud) gets 200 on GET /api/v1/users instead of 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="...", error="invalid_token".

title: Missing/malformed Authorization header 401 lacks the WWW-Authenticate challenge
observable: GET /api/v1/users with no Authorization header (or "Basic abc") returns 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} but with no WWW-Authenticate header, instead of WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="<audience>".

title: Login rate limiter off by one: 5th attempt in a window is throttled
observable: Five POST /login attempts with the same username and a wrong password within a minute: the 5th returns 429 {"error":"too many login attempts"} with Retry-After, instead of 401 (only the 6th should be 429). Per-client: 20th request is 429 instead of 21st.

title: Login accepts the request if either username or password is correct
observable: POST /login {"username":"<AUTH_USERNAME>","password":"wrong"} returns 200 {"token":"..."} (a token that works on /api/v1/users) instead of 401. Likewise a wrong username with the correct password.

title: Login token expiry hard-coded to 24h instead of JWT_TTL
observable: POST /login with valid credentials returns a token whose decoded payload has exp - iat = 86400 seconds instead of JWT_TTL (15m = 900 seconds).

title: UPDATE predicate uses >= so all rows at or after the target id are renamed
observable: With users ids 1..3, PUT /api/v1/users/2 {"name":"Zed"} returns 200 with {id:"2",name:"Zed"}, but the users table now has rows 2 AND 3 named 'Zed'; GET /api/v1/users/3 shows "Zed".

title: JSON content-type check compares the raw header, rejecting parameters such as charset
observable: POST /api/v1/users with Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 and a valid body returns 415 {"error":"Content-Type must be application/json"} instead of 201. Also affects PUT and POST /login.

title: CORS reflects any Origin instead of only the allowlist
observable: With CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS empty, GET /api/v1/users (or OPTIONS preflight with Access-Control-Request-Method) sent with Origin: https://evil.example returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example plus Allow-Methods/Allow-Headers, instead of no CORS headers.
